Segment-tree point toggles update the exact current answer from the initial(c,z)=(1,1), without rebuilding bracket strings.

targets.review_note: Inject1 ampere at A and ground B, build the conductance Laplacian, and solve Kirchhoff equations with pivoted Gaussian elimination. The voltage at A is the equivalent resistance. Parallel conductances add naturally, dangling branches carry zero net current, and disconnected irrelevant components are excluded. This covers all guaranteed series/parallel inputs without fragile local simplification ordering.

targets.review_note: Partition the triangular lattice of hexagon centers into six60-degree sectors, including exactly one boundary ray per sector. In one sector write center=(3a/2,sqrt(3)(a+2b)/2) with a>=1,b>=0. The farthest hexagon vertex is at(1/2,sqrt(3)/2), giving (3a+1)^2+3(a+2b+1)^2<=4k^2. Exact integer square roots count b values; add the central cell and multiply sector count by6.

targets.review_note: Two Dijkstra runs give each branch total round-trip distance to headquarters. A group of size k costs(k-1) times the sum of those distances. By exchanging branches between group sizes an optimum has contiguous groups in sorted-distance order. Prefix sums evaluate segment cost; its Monge property gives monotone split indices for divide-and-conquer partition DP. Directed outward and return distances are kept separate until summed.

targets.review_note: Sweep chairs left-to-right while tracking the number of directed path components. Endpoint charges include signed coordinates so every eventual edge receives its absolute distance plus takeoff/landing costs. Ordinary vertices open, extend, or merge components; start/end have only one incident path edge. Availability checks account for components lacking an incoming/outgoing endpoint. Prohibit joining the start-to-end component before the final chair, preventing disconnected premature completion and cycles.
